blocks.body: Birth and adoption trigger a special enrollment period: at least 30 days for an employer group plan and 60 days on the Marketplace. Enrolling within it can cover the child from the date of birth or adoption; missing it can mean waiting for the next open enrollment. Medicaid and CHIP take applications at any time of year, and a baby born to a mother on Medicaid is covered until the first birthday without a separate application. Moving to family HDHP coverage also changes your HSA limit.
blocks.plain: A birth or adoption gives you a special window to add your child to health coverage: at least 30 days for a job-based plan and 60 days on the Marketplace. If you sign up in time, coverage can start on the day of the birth or adoption. Miss it and you may have to wait for the next open enrollment. You can apply for Medicaid and CHIP any time of year, and a baby born to a mother on Medicaid is covered until the first birthday without a separate application. If you switch to family coverage on a high-deductible plan, your HSA limit changes too.

The deemed-newborn rule needs the mother to have been on Medicaid (or CHIP as a pregnant woman) on the date of birth; CHIP-only coverage of children in working families is not stated as a rule (see unverified).

blocks.body: You need the child's Social Security number to claim the Child Tax Credit (up to {{fig:ctc_per_child}} per child), and you, or one spouse on a joint return, need an SSN valid for work too. It is usually requested at the hospital with the birth registration. If you owe little or no tax, at most {{fig:ctc_refundable_max}} per child comes back as a refund, and less, or nothing, on low earnings, so also check the Earned Income Tax Credit. While an adoption is pending and the child has no SSN, Form W-7A gets a temporary number to claim the child as a dependent, but not the Child Tax Credit.
blocks.plain: To claim the Child Tax Credit (up to {{fig:ctc_per_child}} per child), your child needs a Social Security number. You, or one spouse if you file jointly, also need a Social Security number that is valid for work. You can usually ask for the child's number at the hospital when you register the birth. If you owe little or no tax, no more than {{fig:ctc_refundable_max}} per child comes back as a refund, and less, or nothing, if you earn little, so also check the Earned Income Tax Credit. If an adoption is not final and you can't get the child an SSN yet, Form W-7A gets you a temporary number to claim the child as a dependent. It does not get you the Child Tax Credit.

blocks.body: A dependent is the main reason to own term life insurance; the common heuristic is 10–12 times the primary earner's income, and the DIME method gives a more specific number. A parent at home or earning less needs coverage too, sized to the childcare and household work that would have to be paid for, and group life through a job usually ends with the job. Your pay now supports a child, so check your disability coverage as well. A will is where you name a guardian for a minor child; without one, a court decides. Update beneficiary designations at the same time, and do not name a minor child directly: money left to a minor can end up with a court-appointed guardian, so name a trust or a custodian under your state's transfers-to-minors law.
blocks.plain: A child who depends on you is the main reason to have term life insurance. A common rule of thumb is 10–12 times the main earner's income; the DIME method gives a number that fits your household. A parent who stays home or earns less needs coverage too, enough to pay for the childcare and housework they do now. Life insurance through your job usually stops when the job ends. Your paycheck now supports a child, so check your disability coverage too. A will is where you name a guardian for a young child — without one, a court chooses. Update the beneficiaries on your accounts at the same time. Don't name a young child as a beneficiary directly: a court may have to appoint someone to hold the money. Name a trust, or a custodian under your state's law for gifts to minors, instead.

blocks.body: A dependent-care FSA, if your employer offers one, shelters childcare costs from income and payroll tax (2026 limit: {{fig:limit_dcfsa}} per household, {{fig:limit_dcfsa_mfs}} if married filing separately). Your plan may let you start or change the election after a birth or adoption, so ask HR right away rather than waiting for open enrollment. Money you set aside but do not spend is generally forfeited, so elect only what you are sure to spend. Expenses reimbursed through the FSA cannot also be counted for the child and dependent care credit, so the two have to be coordinated rather than both maxed.
blocks.plain: A dependent-care FSA lets you pay for childcare with money that skips income and payroll tax, if your employer offers one (2026 limit: {{fig:limit_dcfsa}} per household, {{fig:limit_dcfsa_mfs}} if married filing separately). Your plan may let you sign up or change the amount after a birth or adoption, so ask HR right away instead of waiting for open enrollment. Money you put in but don't spend is usually lost, so only put in what you are sure to spend. Costs you pay through the FSA can't also count toward the child and dependent care credit. So plan the two together instead of trying to max both.

blocks.body: 529 plans grow tax-free for qualified education costs, and about 30 states offer a state income tax deduction for contributions. The framework places education saving after the tax-advantaged retirement steps, because a student can borrow for college and a retiree cannot borrow for retirement.

draft.title: Plan the leave and the pay gap
draft.body: The drop in pay during leave is often the first money event. The federal FMLA gives eligible employees up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period for a birth or adoption, but the leave may be unpaid, and it asks for 30 days' notice when the date is foreseeable. Pay during leave may come from employer leave, short-term disability or a state paid-leave program if your state has one; check each one's claim rules before the due date.
draft.plain: Your pay may drop while you are on leave, and that is often the first money problem. The federal FMLA lets eligible workers take up to 12 workweeks of leave in a 12-month period for a birth or adoption and keep their job, but that leave can be unpaid. It asks you to tell your employer 30 days ahead when you know the date. Pay during leave can come from your employer's leave, short-term disability, or your state's paid-leave program if it has one. Check how to claim each one before the due date.
props: Pay drop during leave is often the first money event
FMLA: up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period for birth or adoption, for eligible employees
Pay sources: employer leave, short-term disability, state paid leave where it exists
Check claim rules before the due date

draft.title: Claim the adoption credit and any employer adoption help
draft.when: The tax year the adoption costs are paid or the adoption is final
draft.body: For 2026 the adoption credit covers qualified adoption expenses up to {{fig:adoption_credit_max}} per child, and up to {{fig:adoption_credit_refundable_max}} of it is refundable. If your employer has an adoption assistance program, those payments can also be excluded from income, but the same expenses cannot count for both. If a state has determined the child has special needs, the full credit can be claimed even with few or no expenses. The credit phases out at higher incomes.
draft.plain: For 2026 the adoption credit can cover adoption costs up to {{fig:adoption_credit_max}} per child, and up to {{fig:adoption_credit_refundable_max}} of it can come back as a refund. If your employer helps pay for adoption, that help can also be left out of your taxable income, but you can't use the same costs for both. If a state says the child has special needs, you can claim the full credit even if you had few or no adoption costs. The credit gets smaller at higher incomes.
props: 2026 adoption credit up to the figures-layer maximum per child
Up to the figures-layer amount is refundable
Employer adoption assistance can be excluded from income
left out of your taxable income
Same expenses cannot count for both
Special-needs adoption (state-determined): the full credit is allowed regardless of expenses
The credit phases out at higher incomes
